Definition: from G575 and G2947; to roll away:--roll away (back).
BiblicalUsage: To roll away — four times, and every time about the stone at the tomb. The women ask on the way in Mark 16:3, who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre, and when they look in Mark 16:4 they see it is already rolled away. They found the stone rolled away in Luke 24:2, and Matthew 28:2 tells how: the angel of the Lord descended from heaven and rolled back the stone and sat upon it.
TheologicalSignificance: I love that the women carried a question they could not answer and found it answered before they arrived. The stone was very great, and it was already moved — the angel did not roll it away to let Jesus out, but to let the women in to see He was gone. Every impossibility I carry to the tomb is already rolled away.
